model.name: Location Referencing / Address
model.purpose: Provide the format-neutral referencing fabric for civic and postal addresses, thoroughfares, geocodes, geographic identifier and grid codes, gazetteer locations, points of interest and place names, independently of the buildings, premises, parcels or people they locate.
model.scope_statement: This mixin governs how a location is designated, encoded, named, assigned, quality-assessed and exchanged. It covers structured civic and postal addresses and their assignment lifecycle; named thoroughfares used in addressing; postal components and rendering; coordinate geocodes and the coordinate reference systems they are expressed in; geographic identifiers including postcodes and open grid codes; linear references along linear objects; gazetteers of location instances; standardised geographical names; and named points of interest used for orientation. Occupancy, ownership, cadastral geometry, building fabric, settlement morphology, indoor topology, person or organisation identity, and the public-law mandate instrument itself belong in sibling models and are referenced, not duplicated.
in_scope: Structured civic, landmark and postal addresses as independent reference objects, including locators, subaddress elements, aliases and status.
Named thoroughfares and related passage features used as address components, including name parts, kind and rename history.
Postal address segments, constructs, elements, country templates and delivery-point identifiers, including post office boxes.
Acts of assigning, maintaining, reassigning and retiring addresses for addressable objects under a public addressing mandate.
Coordinate point encodings, uncertainty, altitude and compact geo identifiers, always with an explicit coordinate reference system.
Geographic identifier schemes, postcodes as spatial codes, and open grid codes such as Open Location Code Plus Codes.
Linear referencing of positions along, and optionally offset from, one-dimensional objects used in addressing and mapping.
Gazetteers of location instances, complementary coordinates, toponyms with language and status, and named points of interest.
Address and location data quality measures, profile crosswalks, privacy, access, retention of historic references, and agent bootstrap.
out_of_scope: The physical building, structure or indoor topology being addressed; those are addressable objects, not addresses.
Premises, occupancy units, tenancy and indoor routing graphs as spatial products.
Cadastral parcels, rights, restrictions and responsibilities; parcels may be addressable objects but are not addresses.
Settlement, district or urban-form geometry except as named address context or gazetteer locations.
The public-law mandate instrument that authorises an address registrar; this model records the resulting addressing authority, not the mandate document.
Person, organisation, addressee or mailee identity beyond postal-segment fields required to render a postal item.
Continuous GNSS observation streams, map cartography, and the full geodetic realisation of a national CRS product.
Proprietary three-word or closed grid products that lack an open, first-party specification aligned here.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Building structure and premises spatial unit models
boundary_notes.distinction: Those models describe the addressable object. This mixin describes the independent civic, postal or coded reference bound to that object; an address can outlive a building and a building can carry several addresses.
A parcel identifier is a cadastral object identifier. An address may be assigned where no building stands, but parcel geometry, tenure and survey are not address semantics.
Settlements and districts supply named geographic context and gazetteer locations. They are not street-level locators, postal templates or geocode observations.

ISO 19160-2 places assignment under public administration and local mandate. The mandate artefact lives in the public-mandate sibling; this model records assigning authority, process and resulting address state.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Person or organisation identity and contact
boundary_notes.distinction: ISO 19160-4 addressee and mailee segments and a telephone-number element serve postal rendering. They are not a substitute for a party model, and ISO 19160-4 explicitly does not cover data protection of personal data.

Unit, room, floor, seat and similar locators are civic subaddress elements in PIDF-LO, CLDXF and INSPIRE locator designators. Indoor topology, connectivity and navigation graphs remain a sibling indoor model.

bundles.name: Addressing
bundles.description: Govern civic, landmark and postal designation of locations as independent reference objects, including thoroughfares, locators, postal rendering and the public assignment lifecycle.
bundles.rationale: ISO 19160-1 treats the address as an independent object with its own lifecycle and aliases, and ISO 19160-2 places assignment under a public mandate, so designation, thoroughfares, postal rendering and assignment belong together rather than inside the addressed object.

layers.name: Civic addresses
layers.description: Structured identification of a fixed location by geographic names and identifiers, independently of a particular encoding syntax.

findings.name: Address identity and classification
findings.description: An address is structured information that allows unambiguous determination of an object for identification and location. INSPIRE and SEMIC require a globally unique address identifier; FGDC treats identifier, class and documentation attributes as first-class; NENA distinguishes civic, postal, service and subaddress types that are not interchangeable.

questions.text: What is the authoritative master-system identifier of this address, which scheme issued it, and is there a governed IRI?
Is this record a civic, postal, landmark, service or mixed address, and which national or application profile of ISO 19160-1 does it implement?
Which alternative or legacy identifiers must be retained for interoperability with existing systems without treating a date as an identifier?
Which register is the identifier master, and may a consuming Dimension mint a UUID only after that master is shown to be absent?

data_elements.name: master-address-id
data_elements.description: Authoritative identifier assigned by the address register

data_elements.name: id-scheme
data_elements.description: Scheme or namespace of the master identifier

data_elements.name: global-iri
data_elements.description: Governed IRI when published as linked data

data_elements.name: dimension-uuid
data_elements.description: UUID or ULID assigned only when no master identifier exists

data_elements.name: address-class
data_elements.description: Civic, postal, landmark, service or mixed classification

data_elements.name: country-code
data_elements.description: Country of the address, INSPIRE administrative unit level 1

data_elements.name: alternative-identifier
data_elements.description: External thematic identifier for legacy interoperability

data_elements.name: profile-id
data_elements.description: National or application profile of ISO 19160-1

artifacts.name: Address register record
artifacts.description: Authoritative persisted address identity, class, identifiers and status
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the master register identifier; a governed IRI where published as linked data; a Dimension UUID or ULID only when no master identifier exists.

findings.name: Address component structure
findings.description: Addresses are composed from hierarchically related components: administrative unit names, address area names, thoroughfare names, postal descriptors and locators. SEMIC/locn and INSPIRE expose thoroughfare, locator designator, locator name, address area, post code, post name, PO box and full address; FGDC additionally taxonomises US thoroughfare, landmark and postal forms.

questions.text: Which administrative units, address area, thoroughfare, locators and postal descriptors constitute this address, and in what combination rule?
What is the complete full-address string, in which language and script, and is it intended for display, print or both?
Which structure, wing, floor, unit, room, section, row or seat locators further specify this civic location without implying an indoor topology model?
Does the governing profile require an administrative unit at country level, as INSPIRE does, and what ISO 3166-1 value is used?

data_elements.name: address-area
data_elements.description: Non-administrative neighbourhood, village or named area

data_elements.name: thoroughfare-name
data_elements.description: Passage name used in the address

data_elements.name: locator-designator
data_elements.description: Building, unit or other numeric or coded locator

data_elements.name: locator-name
data_elements.description: Proper name of the located feature

data_elements.name: full-address
data_elements.description: Complete address as a single string

artifacts.name: Address component set
artifacts.description: Structured breakdown of one address into components with language and level
artifacts.identity_strategy: Bound to the master address identifier of the address it decomposes; components carry no independent master identity.

findings.name: Address lifecycle and aliases
findings.description: ISO 19160-1 includes lifecycle, metadata and aliases in the conceptual model. ISO 19160-2 treats assignment, component change, reassignment to a different object and retirement as maintenance. INSPIRE records beginLifespanVersion, and related validity attributes, for the spatial-object version. Aliases are not a second identity.

questions.text: What is the current status, real-world valid-from and valid-to, and database lifespan-version timestamps, each in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z?
Which aliases, former numbers or multilingual forms must continue to resolve to this address without minting a new master identifier?
What was the real-world event time of the status change, and what was the distinct observation or ingestion time?
If retired, is the identifier retained as history, and under what explicit reassignment event may it be bound to a different object?

data_elements.name: status
data_elements.description: Proposed, current, retired, reserved or equivalent local code

data_elements.name: valid-to
data_elements.description: End of real-world validity if known

data_elements.name: lifespan-version-begin
data_elements.description: Database version insertion or change time

data_elements.name: alias-value
data_elements.description: Alternative designation for the same address

data_elements.name: alias-type
data_elements.description: Former name, multilingual form, unofficial or spelling variant

artifacts.name: Address version record
artifacts.description: One lifespan version of an address with validity and alias set
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master address identifier plus the lifespan-version begin timestamp in RFC 3339; the timestamp qualifies the version and is never the identifier alone.

layers.name: Thoroughfares
layers.description: Named streets, roads, waterways and other passages that supply the thoroughfare component of civic addresses and may be renamed independently of abutting addresses.

findings.name: Thoroughfare identity, naming and extent
findings.description: A thoroughfare is an address component representing a passage from one location to another and is not necessarily a road; it may be a waterway or other feature. RFC 5139 adds a road hierarchy (name, section, branch, sub-branch, pre- and post-modifiers). FGDC treats thoroughfare names as a managed class with documentation and linear reference locations. Renaming is an ISO 19160-2 maintenance event.

questions.text: What is the master thoroughfare identifier, official name parts, language and thoroughfare kind?
Are section, branch, sub-branch or pre/post-modifiers required to disambiguate this thoroughfare in the local civic scheme?
When was this thoroughfare renamed, what former names remain aliases, and which addresses were affected without automatically changing their master identifiers?
Is a centreline, linear-reference axis or other extent recorded for mapping, and in which CRS, without turning this record into a transport-network product?

data_elements.name: thoroughfare-kind
data_elements.description: Road, path, waterway or other passage

data_elements.name: former-name
data_elements.description: Name superseded by a rename event

artifacts.name: Thoroughfare record
artifacts.description: Named passage with identifiers, name parts, kind and rename history
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the master thoroughfare identifier issued by the naming authority; former names are retained as aliases rather than as new identities.

layers.name: Postal delivery
layers.description: Postal components, country templates and delivery-point constructs used to render and route postal items, aligned to ISO 19160-4 / UPU S42.

findings.name: Postal components, templates and delivery points
findings.description: ISO 19160-4, based on UPU S42 Version 8, organises postal address components into segments, constructs and elements, specifies rendering templates, and does not specify component lengths or value ranges. Addressee and mailee segments are optional postal functions, not civic location. A post office box is a delivery-point designator and may have no public civic location. NENA warns that a postal address is frequently not valid for emergency service.

questions.text: Which ISO 19160-4 segments, constructs and elements are populated, and is an addressee or mailee stored as postal data rather than as a party master?
Which country template, line-selection conditions and space constraints produce the rendered postal lines?
Is the delivery target a post office box or other non-site delivery point, and is a separate civic or service address required for physical location?
Has an emergency-location profile rejected this postal form, and if so which civic or service address replaces it?

data_elements.name: postal-segment-set
data_elements.description: Addressee, mailee, despatching, delivery segments present

data_elements.name: rendered-lines
data_elements.description: Ordered output lines after template application

data_elements.name: addressee-present
data_elements.description: Whether an addressee segment is stored

artifacts.name: Postal render record
artifacts.description: Template identifier, selected components and rendered lines for a postal item
artifacts.identity_strategy: Derived from the referenced civic or postal address identifier plus the country template identifier and rendering time; it mints no location master identifier.

layers.name: Assignment and governance
layers.description: Assign, maintain, reassign and retire addresses for objects in the physical world under a documented public mandate and role set.

findings.name: Address assignment, maintenance and authority
findings.description: During assignment an address is first associated with a particular object in the physical world. During maintenance it may be reassigned, have components modified, or be retired. Local governments commonly hold the mandate, supported by national government, postal agencies and others. FGDC introduces an address reference system as the formal description of local assignment rules. Signage installation is in scope of ISO 19160-2 as a physical-world process, not as a building product.

questions.text: Which addressable object is currently bound to this address, of what object type, and is the bind 1:1, 1:n or n:1?
Which organisation holds the addressing mandate, under which instrument, and which address reference system encodes local numbering and naming rules?
What assignment, component-change, reassignment or retirement event occurred, at what event time, on what basis, and at what distinct ingestion time?
Have address-component signs been installed or updated in the physical world as part of the ISO 19160-2 process, and who is responsible for that installation?

data_elements.name: addressable-object-ref
data_elements.description: Building, premises, parcel or other addressable object

data_elements.name: address-reference-system-id
data_elements.description: Local ruleset for numbering and naming

data_elements.name: signage-status
data_elements.description: Whether physical signs have been installed

artifacts.name: Address assignment event
artifacts.description: Act binding an address to an addressable object with authority, basis and time
artifacts.identity_strategy: Assignment event identifier issued by the assigning authority, qualified by the RFC 3339 event time; identifier reuse requires an explicit reassignment event.

bundles.name: Geocoding
bundles.description: Represent locations by coordinates, geographic identifiers and linear measures, always with the system in which those values are expressed.
bundles.rationale: ISO 19111 makes coordinates ambiguous without a stated CRS and ISO 19112 separates identifier-based referencing from coordinate referencing, so encodings, reference systems, codes and linear measures are governed as one referencing surface.

layers.name: Coordinate geocodes
layers.description: Point coordinate values, uncertainty, altitude and compact geo encodings for a location.

findings.name: Coordinate point, precision and encoding
findings.description: A geocode in this model is a coordinate or code representation of a location. RFC 5870 defines a protocol-independent geo URI for a single point, defaulting to WGS-84, with optional altitude and uncertainty; civic addresses and complex geometries are out of its scope. ISO 19111 makes coordinates without a CRS ambiguous. locn allows WKT, GML, geo URI, GeoHash and schema encodings as interchangeable geometry carriers.

questions.text: What are the coordinate values, including any height or depth, and in which CRS are they expressed?
What uncertainty or precision is claimed, by which method, and at what observation time distinct from ingestion time?
Is a geo URI or other compact encoding published, and does it use the WGS-84 default or an explicitly registered crs parameter?
How many geocodes of differing precision, method or CRS are attached to the same address or gazetteer location, and which is the default geographic position?

data_elements.name: height-or-depth
data_elements.description: Optional height or depth with unit

data_elements.name: crs-id
data_elements.description: CRS identifier, for example EPSG 4326 or 4979

data_elements.name: geometry-encoding
data_elements.description: WKT, GML, geo URI or other declared encoding

artifacts.name: Geocode observation
artifacts.description: One coordinate or compact encoding with CRS, uncertainty, method and observation time
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the referenced address or location instance plus method, CRS and RFC 3339 observation time; several observations may coexist with one flagged as default position.

layers.name: Reference systems
layers.description: Identify and govern the coordinate reference systems and operations used to interpret geocodes.

findings.name: CRS identity, dynamics and operations
findings.description: ISO 19111 defines the minimum data required to describe spatial, parametric, temporal and mixed CRS, including local engineering CRS, CRS attached to moving platforms, and dynamic CRS whose coordinate values change with tectonic motion. The CRS definition itself does not change with time. Coordinate operations change coordinate values between CRS. RFC 5870 equates default WGS-84 with EPSG 4326 and 4979 and discourages arbitrary alternate CRS when comparison matters.

questions.text: Which CRS identifier and register authority interpret this geocode, and is that CRS spatial, engineering, dynamic, parametric, temporal or compound?
If the CRS is dynamic, what coordinate epoch applies, and must the geocode be revised as crustal motion accumulates?
Which coordinate operation transforms this value to the exchange CRS used for comparison, and who is responsible for applying it?
Is this an engineering CRS for a site or a CRS on a moving platform, and to which Earth-fixed CRS does it relate?

data_elements.name: crs-kind
data_elements.description: Geodetic, projected, engineering, dynamic, parametric, temporal or compound

data_elements.name: operation-id
data_elements.description: Coordinate operation to an exchange CRS

data_elements.name: exchange-crs-id
data_elements.description: CRS used for comparison and publication

artifacts.name: CRS register entry
artifacts.description: Identified CRS with authority, kind, epoch and declared operations
artifacts.identity_strategy: Referenced by the external CRS register identifier and authority, for example EPSG; this mixin never mints CRS identifiers.

layers.name: Geographic identifier codes
layers.description: Indirect spatial references by label or code, including postcodes, gazetteer codes and open grid codes.

findings.name: Geographic identifiers and grid codes
findings.description: ISO 19112 defines spatial referencing by geographic identifiers as a label or code that identifies a location, with country names and postcodes as examples, and distinguishes this from coordinate referencing. Open Location Code Plus Codes encode an area, not a point, can be generated and decoded offline, and are designed as a replacement for street addresses where streets are unnamed. Shortened plus codes require a nearby reference location to recover the full code.

questions.text: Which geographic-identifier scheme and value designate this location, and is the value a label, a postcode, a grid code or another code type?
Does the code represent an area rather than a point, and what is the implied cell size or plus-code length?
If a shortened Plus Code is stored, what reference location is required to recover the full code, and is that reference a coordinate or a named place?
Is this identifier used because no civic address exists, and what is the relationship to any later-assigned civic address?

data_elements.name: identifier-scheme
data_elements.description: Postcode, plus-code, national grid or other scheme

data_elements.name: area-not-point
data_elements.description: True when the code denotes an area

data_elements.name: plus-code-length
data_elements.description: Digit length controlling Plus Code area

data_elements.name: short-code-reference
data_elements.description: Reference location used to shorten or recover a Plus Code

data_elements.name: substitutes-for-civic-address
data_elements.description: Whether the code is used in lieu of a civic address

artifacts.name: Geographic identifier record
artifacts.description: Scheme, value, area semantics and recovery parameters for an indirect spatial reference
artifacts.identity_strategy: Scheme plus code value as issued by the identifier authority; Plus Codes are computed from coordinates and are not minted by a register.

layers.name: Linear referencing
layers.description: Locate events and points by measure along, and optionally offset from, a one-dimensional object such as a thoroughfare.

findings.name: Linear position along addressing features
findings.description: FGDC requires attributes for linear reference locations as part of address documentation and mapping. This finding records measure-along and optional offset against a thoroughfare or other linear object used in addressing. A dedicated ISO 19148 linear-referencing schema exists as an alignment target; the full transportation-network product remains a sibling. Absence of a fetched ISO 19148 abstract in this run is recorded as a coverage gap for operation detail.

questions.text: Which linear object, typically a thoroughfare axis, is the reference, and what identifier and direction apply?
What measure, unit and start referent locate the point or event along that object?
What offset, side and unit place the address relative to the linear object, for example building set-back from centreline?
Is this linear location documentation of an existing civic address, or a substitute where no locator designator exists?

data_elements.name: measure
data_elements.description: Distance or chainage along the object

data_elements.name: from-referent
data_elements.description: Start referent if not the object origin

artifacts.name: Linear reference location
artifacts.description: Measure and offset of an address or event along a named linear object
artifacts.identity_strategy: Composite of the linear element identifier, start referent and measure; it documents an address rather than carrying an address master identifier.

bundles.name: Named places
bundles.description: Gazetteer locations, standardised geographical names and named points of interest used for orientation, discovery and indirect spatial reference.
bundles.rationale: ISO 19112 location instances and UNGEGN name standardisation supply indirect spatial reference and orientation that addresses and coordinates alone do not provide, and they are maintained by different authorities.

layers.name: Gazetteer
layers.description: Register of location instances of one or more location types, with optional complementary coordinates.

findings.name: Gazetteer location instances
findings.description: ISO 19112 specifies a conceptual scheme for a gazetteer as a register of location instances of one or more location sub-types, containing some information regarding position, which need not be coordinates. Geographic identifiers provide indirect spatial reference. Complementary coordinate references may be recorded without converting the gazetteer into a coordinate-only product. SEMIC Location is any identifiable geographic place and may be named, addressed, geometrically described, or identified by URI.

questions.text: What is the location-instance identifier, location type and geographic identifier, and which gazetteer authority maintains it?
Is position recorded as description, complementary coordinates, both, or neither, and in which CRS if coordinates exist?
Is a governed URI from a names register published for this location, and how does it relate to the address identifier if both exist?
Which ISO 19112 spatial reference system using geographic identifiers defines the parent locations and location types for this gazetteer?

data_elements.name: geographic-identifier
data_elements.description: Label, code or URI for the location

artifacts.name: Gazetteer entry
artifacts.description: One location instance with type, identifier, names and optional complementary position
artifacts.identity_strategy: Location-instance identifier issued by the gazetteer authority, with the geographic identifier as the indirect spatial reference and a governed URI where published.

layers.name: Place names
layers.description: Toponyms with language, script, status and authority, including endonyms, exonyms and romanisation.

findings.name: Toponyms, language, status and authority
findings.description: UNGEGN is mandated to encourage national standardisation of geographical names, dissemination of nationally standardised names, and adoption of single romanisation systems. locn geographicName explicitly allows endonym, romanisation and exonym forms, using the INSPIRE example of Αθήνα, Athína and Athens. Name status and language are required to prevent treating variant spellings as separate places.

questions.text: What is the standardised endonym, in which language and script, and which national names authority issued it?
Which exonyms and romanised forms are published, under which romanisation system, and which are preferred for international exchange?
Is the name official, historical or deprecated, and from when to when, without using the date as the name identifier?
Does this toponym name a settlement, thoroughfare, POI, hydrologic feature or other gazetteer type, and is homonym disambiguation required?

data_elements.name: name-status
data_elements.description: Official, standardised, historical, deprecated or unofficial

data_elements.name: romanisation-system
data_elements.description: UNGEGN or other romanisation system if applicable

artifacts.name: Toponym record
artifacts.description: One authorised or variant geographical name with language, script, type and status
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the named feature reference plus name string, language tag and name type; variant spellings are name records, not separate places.

layers.name: Points of interest
layers.description: Named points of interest used for orientation and discovery, stewarded as gazetteer locations with weaker dedicated international standardisation than addresses.

findings.name: Points of interest as named locations
findings.description: No ISO addressing part defines a dedicated POI class equivalent to Address. SEMIC Location and ISO 19112 location instances can represent named places of public or historical interest. Category vocabularies, opening-hours and commercial listing agreements are not standardised by the primary sources in this run and must be treated as local extensions. Subject-owner stewardship of a POI listing is an operating pattern, not a normative ISO requirement.

questions.text: What identifier and primary name identify this point of interest, and is it a gazetteer location instance rather than a separate product class?
What category vocabulary and value apply, what is the operating status, and is that vocabulary locally governed rather than ISO-standard?
Which address, geocode or gazetteer location situates the POI, and may it resolve to more than one address?
Is a subject owner authorised to create or update this listing, under what publication agreement, and who remains the gazetteer authority?

data_elements.name: category
data_elements.description: Local category code; vocabulary is a gap

data_elements.name: related-address-id
data_elements.description: Civic or postal address if any

artifacts.name: POI record
artifacts.description: Named place used for discovery, with category, status and links to address or geocode
artifacts.identity_strategy: POI identifier held as a gazetteer location instance identifier; it never substitutes for the civic address master identifier.

bundles.name: Quality, interoperability and stewardship
bundles.description: Measure address and location data quality, record profile conflicts, and govern access, privacy, retention and agent bootstrap.
bundles.rationale: ISO 19160-3 defines address quality without prescribing a minimum level and ISO 19160-1 is only a cross-map hub, so fitness for use, crosswalk conflicts and access, privacy and retention rules must be governed explicitly rather than assumed.

layers.name: Address data quality
layers.description: Describe, measure and report quality of address data without imposing a universal minimum quality level.

findings.name: Quality elements, measures and reporting
findings.description: ISO 19160-3 is a profile of ISO 19157 that establishes data quality elements and measures for address data, procedures for reporting, and guidelines for use. Elements include completeness, logical consistency, positional accuracy, temporal quality, thematic accuracy and usability. The standard does not define minimum acceptable quality; fitness depends on use.

questions.text: Against which dataset or record scope, product specification and intended use was quality evaluated?
What completeness, logical consistency, positional accuracy, temporal quality, thematic accuracy and usability results were obtained?
When was the evaluation performed, by which method, and is the result still current relative to subsequent updates?
Does the consumer impose a minimum quality threshold that ISO 19160-3 itself does not define, and is that threshold recorded as a local constraint?

data_elements.name: quality-scope
data_elements.description: Dataset, series or record scope of the evaluation

data_elements.name: logical-consistency-result
data_elements.description: Conceptual, domain, format and topological consistency

artifacts.name: Address quality report
artifacts.description: Evaluation results against ISO 19160-3 elements for a stated scope and use
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by evaluated scope, product specification and RFC 3339 evaluation time; a new evaluation adds a report rather than altering address identity.

layers.name: Profile alignment
layers.description: Cross-map between ISO 19160-1, INSPIRE, FGDC, CLDXF, locn and postal templates without claiming unproven conformance.

findings.name: Profile crosswalk and conflicts
findings.description: ISO 19160-1 is explicitly a common representation for cross-mapping, not a replacement of other conceptual models. INSPIRE Address is a legal spatial object with required country component and default geographic position. FGDC is a general-purpose US repository standard. CLDXF-US is a PIDF-LO profile for emergency location and is not equivalent to USPS postal form. SEMIC locn is more flexible than INSPIRE and not reversible to full INSPIRE structure. Civic, postal and service addresses can disagree for the same site.

questions.text: Which source profile stores the record and which target profile does the consumer require?
Which documented conflicts apply, including civic versus postal versus emergency service address, missing country component, or indoor locators absent from a postal template?
Is conversion lossless, lossy or not-mappable, and which elements would be dropped or invented if conversion proceeded?
Is any conformance claim limited to alignment, or is there evidence of passing an abstract test suite such as INSPIRE or ISO 19160-4?

artifacts.name: Profile crosswalk
artifacts.description: Documented mapping and conflict log between two address or location profiles
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the ordered pair of source and target profile identifiers plus the mapping rule identifier.

layers.name: Access, privacy and retention
layers.description: Govern who may read or change location references, how precise location is protected, and how historic addresses are retained or erased.

findings.name: Privacy, access and historic retention
findings.description: RFC 5870 treats invalid locations and location privacy as security considerations. ISO 19160-4 reminds implementers that storage and exchange of personal data are subject to legislation and is silent on a data-protection method. Retired addresses should be retained as history under ISO 19160-2 rather than destroyed by default, except where a legal erasure right applies to personal addressee data or high-precision coordinates. Open gazetteer publication is a projection that omits occupancy and ownership.

questions.text: Is this record in the public gazetteer projection, restricted, emergency-only or private, and which licence covers public release?
What coordinate precision or uncertainty is published to non-privileged consumers, and is the full-precision value retained under a tighter scope?
Does the record contain addressee, mailee, telephone or other personal data in the postal sense, and which data-protection regime applies?
On withdrawal, is the address retired and retained as history, or is a legal erasure of personal or precise-location data required, and what audit is kept?

data_elements.name: publication-class
data_elements.description: Public gazetteer, restricted, emergency-only or private

data_elements.name: precision-reduction
data_elements.description: Rounding or uncertainty applied for public release

data_elements.name: personal-data-flag
data_elements.description: Whether addressee or other personal data is stored

data_elements.name: erasure-basis
data_elements.description: Legal basis if a delete rather than retire is required

data_elements.name: licence
data_elements.description: Publication licence for the gazetteer projection

artifacts.name: Gazetteer publication policy
artifacts.description: Access class, precision reduction, licence, retention and erasure rules for location references
artifacts.identity_strategy: Held by the publishing gazetteer or registrar authority and identified by that authority plus publication class; it governs records rather than identifying a location.

functions.name: Assign address
functions.description: Bind a new or existing address to an addressable object under the addressing mandate, recording basis, event time and ingestion time.
inputs: Address components or existing address identifier
preconditions: The actor holds or is delegated the public addressing mandate
effects: The address is bound to the addressable object
Real-world event time and ingestion time are recorded separately

functions.name: Maintain address
functions.description: Modify address components, reassign the address to a different object, or retire it while retaining identifier history.
preconditions: The address exists in the register
effects: Components are modified, the address is reassigned, or the address is retired

functions.name: Rename thoroughfare
functions.description: Record an official thoroughfare name change, preserve former names as aliases, and identify affected addresses without silently changing their master identifiers.
preconditions: The actor is the thoroughfare naming authority
effects: Former names remain resolvable as aliases
Affected addresses are identified without automatic master-identifier change

functions.name: Render postal address
functions.description: Apply an ISO 19160-4 / UPU S42 template to produce ordered postal lines for a stated country and space constraint.
preconditions: A country template exists for the destination
effects: Postal lines are produced under the selected template's line-selection conditions

functions.name: Forward geocode
functions.description: Derive one or more coordinate or grid-code geocodes for an address or place, each with CRS, method, precision and observation time.
outputs: Geocode observations with CRS, method, precision and observation time
preconditions: A CRS is declared for each derived coordinate
effects: Geocode observations are attached to the address or location instance

functions.name: Reverse geocode
functions.description: Resolve a coordinate or geographic identifier to candidate addresses or gazetteer locations, returning ranked matches and quality.
inputs: Coordinate with CRS or geographic identifier
outputs: Ranked candidate addresses or gazetteer locations
preconditions: The input coordinate names its CRS
effects: Candidate matches are returned with quality indications

functions.name: Encode or recover Plus Code
functions.description: Encode coordinates to a full Open Location Code, shorten relative to a reference location, or recover a short code.
inputs: Reference location for shortening or recovery
outputs: Full Open Location Code or shortened code
preconditions: A nearby reference location is available when shortening or recovering a short code
effects: A code denoting an area is produced, shortened or recovered

functions.name: Transform coordinates
functions.description: Apply a declared ISO 19111 coordinate operation into an exchange CRS, including epoch handling for dynamic CRS.
outputs: Coordinates expressed in the exchange CRS
preconditions: A declared coordinate operation to the exchange CRS exists
effects: Coordinate values are changed to the exchange CRS with epoch handled

functions.name: Evaluate address quality
functions.description: Measure completeness, logical consistency, positional accuracy, temporal quality, thematic accuracy and usability for a stated scope and use.
preconditions: An intended use is stated, because no universal minimum quality is defined
effects: Quality results are recorded for the stated scope and use

functions.name: Crosswalk profile
functions.description: Map an address or location record between ISO 19160-1 profiles, INSPIRE, FGDC, CLDXF, locn or postal templates, recording lossiness and conflicts.
preconditions: A documented mapping rule exists between the two profiles
effects: Dropped or unmappable elements are recorded rather than invented

functions.name: Publish gazetteer projection
functions.description: Release the authorised public list of addresses, names and places with status, omitting occupancy, ownership and reduced-precision exceptions.
inputs: Authorised addresses, standardised names and location instances
preconditions: Publication class, licence and precision-reduction rules are determined
effects: Occupancy and ownership are omitted from the projection
Coordinate precision is reduced where policy requires

functions.name: Lookup gazetteer
functions.description: Resolve a geographic identifier, toponym or address identifier to location instances, names and complementary positions.
inputs: Geographic identifier, toponym or address identifier
outputs: Location instances, names and complementary positions
preconditions: The gazetteer or names register is accessible to the requesting role
effects: The indirect spatial reference is resolved to location instances

composition.purpose: Buildings and structures are addressable objects that may receive one or more addresses; this mixin does not model fabric, storeys as construction, or demolition as a building event except as a trigger for address maintenance.
Premises and occupancy units are addressable via subaddress locators; unit, room and floor values live here as locators, not as the premises product.
Parcels may be addressed where no building stands; cadastral identity, geometry and rights remain outside this mixin.
Settlements and districts provide named context, address areas and gazetteer locations rather than street locators.
The address registrar operates under a public addressing mandate; the mandate instrument is a sibling, the resulting assignment authority is this model.
Adopt the ISO 19160-1 conceptual model, lifecycle and alias constructs as the cross-map hub, without claiming to replace national profiles.
Align postal segments, elements, codes and rendering templates; do not treat postal addressee as the location master.
Use ISO 19112 for gazetteers and geographic-identifier spatial reference systems, including complementary coordinates.
Every coordinate geocode must name a CRS and may name a coordinate operation; this mixin does not maintain the geodetic CRS product.
Align to INSPIRE Address spatial objects, required country component, default geographic position and lifespan versioning for European public-sector exchange.
Align US thoroughfare, landmark and postal content, classification, quality tests, address reference system and linear-reference documentation.
Align emergency civic location, thoroughfare hierarchy and indoor locators; never assume postal validity equals emergency validity.
Align toponym standardisation, romanisation and national names-authority practice.
Treat Plus Codes as geographic identifier codes that encode areas and may substitute for civic addresses where none exist.
Use ISO 19160-3 measures as the address-specific profile of ISO 19157 geographic data quality.

owner_package_requirements: The owning package for civic addresses and thoroughfares must be operated by, or delegated from, the organisation that holds the public addressing mandate.
Gazetteer and names authorities own location instances, location types and standardised toponyms; the package references but does not re-master them.
CRS identifiers are owned by external registers such as EPSG; the package must reference register identifiers and never mint its own CRS identity.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Identifiers carry the namespace of the issuing register — address register, gazetteer, national names authority or CRS register — and a governed IRI is used where the record is published as linked data; a Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID namespace is used only when the master identifier is demonstrably absent.
registry_links: Address register of the mandate-holding authority as identifier master for civic addresses and thoroughfares
ISO 19112 gazetteer and national names registers for location instances and toponyms
CRS registers such as EPSG for coordinate reference system identifiers

canonicalization_rules: All timestamps are canonicalised to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z, with real-world event time and observation or ingestion time kept as separate values.
Every stored coordinate value canonically names its CRS, and its coordinate epoch when the CRS is dynamic; comparison across records is invalid without them.
Every name value canonically carries its language tag, and its script and name type where the form is an exonym or romanisation.
patch_rules: Withdrawn addresses are patched by retire-and-retain, not by physical delete, except where a documented legal erasure right applies.
Component change, reassignment to a different object and retirement are recorded as explicit maintenance events with event and ingestion times, never as silent field overwrites.
Aliases, former thoroughfare names and historic toponyms are added as alias or superseded records and must remain resolvable; they never replace the master identifier.
compatibility_rules: ISO 19160-1 is the cross-map hub; conversions between profiles record lossiness and the elements that would be dropped or invented.
Alignment with INSPIRE, FGDC, CLDXF, locn or UPU templates is not conformance unless a test suite result is recorded.
Civic, postal and emergency-service classes are not interchangeable; a consumer must request the class it needs rather than accept a substitute.

identity_priority: Use the authoritative master-system identifier issued by the address register, gazetteer, names authority or CRS register first.
Then a governed global identifier or IRI where the record is published as linked data.
Then a UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, only when the master identifier is demonstrably absent; a date is not an identifier.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All timestamps use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z. Record real-world event time and observation or ingestion time as separate values whenever both exist.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artefacts — address version records, assignment events, geocode observations, postal renders and quality reports — are named by the master identifier of the referenced address, thoroughfare or location instance plus the RFC 3339 event, observation or evaluation time; the timestamp qualifies the series member and never serves as the identifier itself.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Persistent identifiers survive status change. Retired addresses, former thoroughfare names and historic toponyms remain resolvable as history. An identifier must not be silently reused for a different object; reuse requires an explicit reassignment event. Every coordinate value must name its CRS. Postal addressee data must not overwrite civic location identity.

policies: Addresses, thoroughfares, geocodes and standardised names are reference assets independent of occupants, owners and current land use.

The default change operation for withdrawn addresses is retire-and-retain, not physical delete, except where a documented legal erasure right applies to personal addressee data or similarly protected precise location.
Civic, postal and emergency-service address classes may disagree for the same site; consumers must request the class they need rather than assume equivalence.
Public gazetteer projections omit occupancy, ownership and, where policy requires, full-precision coordinates.
ISO 19160-1 is the cross-map hub; alignment with INSPIRE, FGDC, CLDXF, locn or UPU templates is not evidence of conformance unless a test suite result is recorded.
Coordinate comparison across records is invalid unless CRS, and coordinate epoch for dynamic CRS, are explicit.

read: Any authenticated agent may read the public gazetteer projection of current addresses, thoroughfares, standardised names and reduced-precision geocodes.
Privileged roles may read full-precision coordinates, historic versions, assignment provenance, emergency service addresses and postal addressee segments.
Quality reports and profile-crosswalk logs are readable by registrar, aggregator and authorised consumer roles.
create: Only the address registrar, or a delegate under the documented mandate, may create civic addresses, thoroughfares and assignment events.
Postal operators may create delivery-point identifiers and rendered postal forms that reference, but do not mint, civic masters.
Gazetteer and names authorities may create location instances and standardised toponyms.
Subject owners may create POI listing proposals that remain unauthoritative until gazetteer or registrar acceptance.
Consuming Dimensions may attach a UUID or ULID only when the master identifier is demonstrably absent.
update: Registrar roles may change address components, status, aliases and assignment binds.
Thoroughfare naming authorities may rename and record former names.
Geocoding services may revise geocode values, precision and method, recording observation time.
Quality evaluators may add or replace quality reports without altering identity.
POI subject owners may update listing attributes within the listing agreement; they may not alter civic address masters.
delete: Hard delete of an address, thoroughfare or toponym identifier is forbidden by default; use retire, deprecate or supersede.
Personal addressee, mailee or telephone elements may be erased where a legal right applies, leaving the civic location intact.
Full-precision coordinates may be redacted from a publication class without deleting the underlying privileged record.
Dimension-assigned UUIDs may be removed only when a master identifier has since been supplied and a redirect is recorded.

roles.name: Address registrar
responsibilities: Assign, maintain, reassign and retire civic addresses under the public mandate.
Steward the address reference system and thoroughfare names used in numbering.
Publish the authoritative gazetteer projection of addresses and status.

roles.name: Postal operator
responsibilities: Maintain postal templates, delivery-point identifiers and PO box designators.
Render addresses according to ISO 19160-4 / UPU S42 country rules.
Must not treat postal validity as emergency or cadastral validity.

roles.name: Gazetteer and names authority
responsibilities: Maintain location instances, location types and standardised toponyms.
Record language, script, endonym, exonym, romanisation and name status.
Coordinate with UNGEGN practice for international dissemination.

roles.name: Emergency location steward
responsibilities: Maintain civic and service addresses for emergency routing using CLDXF or equivalent PIDF-LO profiles.
Preserve indoor locators required for dispatch.
Flag postal-only records as unfit for emergency use.

roles.name: Geodetic and geocoding operator
responsibilities: Declare CRS, epoch and coordinate operations for every geocode.
Revise coordinates when method, precision or dynamic epoch requires.
Encode and recover open grid codes without substituting them silently for civic masters.

roles.name: Consuming agent
responsibilities: Read AGENTS.md before any other interface.
Request the address class, CRS and publication precision required for the task.
Must not mint a competing master identifier when a register identifier exists.

access.default_rule: Current public gazetteer attributes of addresses, thoroughfares, standardised names and reduced-precision geocodes are readable; assignment provenance, full-precision coordinates, emergency service addresses, postal addressee segments and historic versions are restricted to named roles.
exceptions: Legal erasure of personal postal addressee data.
Emergency-only indoor locators and service addresses.
Precision reduction or withholding of coordinates for protected sites.
Embargoed assignment events before public announcement of a street name or numbering scheme.
audit_requirements: Every create, status change, reassignment, geocode revision, quality evaluation and privileged read of full-precision or personal location data must record actor, role, event time and ingestion time.
Identifier reuse without an explicit reassignment event is an integrity incident.

coverage.claim: This mixin covers the defensible operating surface for location referencing as an independent fabric: ISO 19160 addressing and assignment, ISO 19112 gazetteers, ISO 19111 CRS, ISO 19160-3 quality, ISO 19160-4 / UPU postal templates, INSPIRE and SEMIC address representations, FGDC US address content, IETF geo URI and PIDF-LO civic forms, NENA CLDXF emergency locators, UNGEGN names mandate, and Open Location Code grid identifiers. It does not claim universal completeness across every national numbering culture, proprietary grid product, or indoor topology standard.

checklist.notes: Master register identifiers, INSPIRE addressID, alternative identifiers, IRI and Dimension UUID/ULID fallback are modelled; dates are excluded as identifiers.
ISO 19160-1 aliases and ISO 19160-2 assignment, component change, reassignment and retirement, plus INSPIRE lifespan versioning.
Binds to addressable objects, thoroughfares, CRS, gazetteer parents, POI-to-address and name-to-feature links; sibling geometry products are referenced not copied.
RFC 3339 event versus observation time, validity intervals, INSPIRE beginLifespanVersion, dynamic CRS epoch.
Assignment basis, geocoding method, quality evaluator, names authority and profile-crosswalk evidence.
Registrar mandate, postal operator, gazetteer authority and optional POI subject-owner listing; occupancy and property ownership are out of scope.
ISO 19160-3 quality elements, FGDC quality-testing intent, and explicit non-claim of untested conformance.
Publication classes, privileged full-precision and emergency scopes, AGENTS.md bootstrap.
Default retire-and-retain; legal erasure limited to personal postal data or similarly protected precise location.
ISO 19160-1 as cross-map hub; alignments to INSPIRE, FGDC, CLDXF, locn, UPU S42 and OLC with documented conflicts.
Civic, postal, landmark, service, geographic-identifier and POI classes.
Uncertainty, plus-code area semantics, default geographic position, public precision reduction.
NENA civic versus postal versus service address and indoor locators.
ISO 19160-4 segments, templates and delivery points.

known_omissions: Full ISO 19160-1 UML class diagrams remain paywalled; component lists are grounded in public abstracts plus INSPIRE/SEMIC properties rather than the complete UML.
UPU S42 Version 8 text is cited through ISO 19160-4 rather than a first-party UPU HTML publication.
ISO 19148 linear-referencing operations were not fetched from iso.org in this run; linear locations are grounded in FGDC and marked as an alignment gap for operations.
What3Words and other proprietary three-word encodings have no open primary specification here and are excluded.
National registers such as UK UPRN/AddressBase, Australia G-NAF, Netherlands BAG, France BAN and AS/NZS 4819 are profiles not modelled instance by instance.
H3, S2, MGRS, GARS, Maidenhead and Geohash are recognised geographic-identifier families but lack dedicated primary fetches in this run except GeoHash as a locn encoding option.
IndoorGML and indoor routing graphs are sibling omissions; only civic locators are in scope.
A dedicated international POI category vocabulary was not found among the primary sources; POI category is a local extension gap.
Physical address-sign assets as built-environment objects are a process in ISO 19160-2, not a signage product model.
Japan chome/banchi and Korea dual jibun/road-name systems are acknowledged as regional numbering cultures, not fully encoded profiles.
conflicts: NENA: a postal address is frequently not valid for emergency service; civic, postal and service addresses can differ for one site.
ISO 19160-1 is a cross-map hub and is not intended to replace other conceptual models; claiming a single global address class is false.
SEMIC locn is more flexible than INSPIRE Address; INSPIRE-conformant detail can be expressed in locn, but the reverse is not generally true.
RFC 5870 excludes civic addresses and complex geometries from geo URI; coordinates and civic references are complementary, not substitutes.
Plus Codes encode areas, not points, and shortened codes are ambiguous without a nearby reference location.
ISO 19160-4 adds telephone number as a postal address element, which collides with a contact/party sibling if treated as location semantics.
WGS-84 default in RFC 5870 versus national projected CRS required by many address maps; comparison without transformation is invalid.
FGDC, CLDXF and USPS Publication 28 share US ancestry but serve repository, emergency-exchange and postal-rendering purposes that still conflict in classification.
regional_assumptions: ISO 19160-2's typical registrar is a local government supported by national and postal agencies; some states use a national address register as master.
Thoroughfare-plus-locator civic form is treated as the common international pattern; it does not cover all numbering cultures.
WGS-84 / EPSG 4326 or 4979 is the default exchange CRS for compact geo identifiers; national mapping CRS remain first-class for local geocodes.
Latin-script postal rendering and ISO 3166-1 country codes are default exchange practice; UNGEGN romanisation is required when the endonym is non-Roman.
European INSPIRE constraints (country component, default geographic position, lifespan versioning) apply to EU public-sector exchange, not globally.
US FGDC and NENA CLDXF content is authoritative for United States thoroughfare taxonomy and NG9-1-1 civic exchange, not for other states.
adversarial_checks: If an agent treats an address as an attribute of a building, it will drop historic addresses after demolition; ISO 19160-2 requires independent assignment and retirement.
If an agent geocodes without a CRS, ISO 19111 and RFC 5870 make the point ambiguous and comparisons unsafe.
If an agent uses a postal form for emergency dispatch, NENA states that postal addresses are frequently invalid for 9-1-1.
If an agent treats a Plus Code as a point coordinate or recovers a short code without a nearby reference, location error follows from the OLC definition.
If an agent deletes retired addresses to tidy a database, provenance and alias resolution required by ISO 19160-1/2 are destroyed.
If an agent claims INSPIRE or ISO 19160-4 conformance solely because locn or FGDC fields are populated, the claim is unevidenced.
